correctness.rationale: For every k>=1 and r in 0..6, the formal identity D(q)^7=D(q^7) mod 7 gives an invertible residue-series transfer and first-two coefficients transfer. The exact 7x14 coefficient table is independently verified by colored-part geometric-product DP and logarithmic-derivative integer recurrence; all 44 excluded (k mod7,r) pairs are refuted by their first two terms. Hirschhorn–Sellers Theorem 1.3 supplies infinite vanishing for the five included pairs. The recurrence and proofs are checked with both boundaries n=0 and n>=0, k=7 as zero-class; one-sample optimality has explicit (3,6). Finite data are only used as exhaustive certificates for the intrinsic finite residue quotient, not extrapolated to unbounded indices.

value.rationale: The classification concerns the complete natural set of modulus-seven progressions and every color count, not an arbitrarily selected small range. It closes the missing necessity for previously published five positive congruence families and establishes a uniform optimal finite stopping rule; two entire color classes have no such progressions. The entire infinite-parameter problem reduces rigorously to seven intrinsic color classes. The small computation is therefore a complete natural quotient census with a sharp mathematical recognition theorem, not a standalone routine table.
